passage:
A rumor spread online that a local park would be closed forever. Many residents became angry before checking the city announcement.
The truth was different. The park would close for three months to repair paths and improve lighting.
A community group posted the correct information with the official schedule. They also explained how residents could give suggestions.
The anger slowly decreased.
The event became a lesson in digital citizenship. Sharing information is easy, but correcting it takes more work. A rumor can run faster than a notice because fear gives it energy.
Before reacting, people should ask one simple question: "Where did this information come from?"
